posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Hans, I wonder if:

You could expose the hologram to laser light for hardening as you do but do it when the hologram is just placed in the water bath such that the fringes are expanded a little while it is hardening.

Or, process the hologram completely as you normally do up to the completion of the water bath. Then soak the hologram in a 3 or 4% concentration of AmDi or KDi in water with a couple of drops of Photo-flo. Then lean the plate against the wall and let it dry for a few minutes (10). Then expose the plate again to your laser light (while moving it) as you do for the post hardening (exact times will have to be measured) and then wash the AmDi out or fix the AmDi out rhen finish processing. This may allow you to red shift. For a blue shift try to let the plate dry after soaking in AmDi for a few hours. Then expose to light and process again.

Not shure if you want to play with this or not but I feel that adding more hardening in a more swollen or shrunken state should surely affect color replay.

I also wonder if after your water soak you soak in a concentration of AmDi in a percentage of alcohol/water, then expose to non coherent light then wash and process that may also cause color changes. I may have to play with this latter idea myself but right now I am in the process of upgrading some of my optics that I have had for +20 years then I want to finish testing the Green silver samples sent to me.

Just some friendly things to try!

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I have found that the concentration of the tuning bath gives color shift direction. The tuning bath should be between 30 and 40% alcohol to water. I find it difficult to red shift but easier to blue shift. My envionment changes so much from day to day and month to month that I can not tell you an actual % for shift. Higher concentration is red, lower is blue. To perform reprocessing, just soak in tuning bath then 100% (90% can be used before 100 to save the 100%). The length of time in the tuning bath helps with the amount of shift. A good starting place is between 15 and 45 seconds. The longer you leave it in the tuning bath the further in that direction the shift is. A higher temperature yields broadband characteristics up to a point. I have found that if I leave it in a high temperature bath for a longer period of time I can get color shift with broadband yielding pastels. Too high a temperature will cause milkyness. Lower temperature with long times causes narrower band.

Try to take one of your yellow holograms cut it in half and put half in a bath of 40% alcohol to water for 45 seconds at room temp with constant agitation. Then put in 100% for 1 minute with constant agitation. Air Dry. Then try the exact same with the other half but use 30% alcohol. Hopefully your shifts will be different.

I also found that shifting blue to red or red to blue is very difficult. I have had most of my success shifting 100nm or so (green to orange or green to blue).

The best way to control color is with concentration of AmDi or KDi and exposure time. And the best way to control broadband vs. narrow band is age of film. and exposure time.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I am not sure how much you want to play.

Did you try water first then the alcohol?

Is it possible to soak the already processed hologram in a chemical hardener, then water then alcohol again? 

Or, soak the already processed hologram in water, then a chemical hardener then alcohol?

You are breaking new ground here! 

For some reason it sounds like the emulsion is softer then regular DCG, so some type of hardening process should keep the milkiness away. That is of course if the "stretching" threshold has not been exceeded. One way to test that is, can you take the milky white reprocessed hologram and get it back to it's original color by repeating your entire process? If it stays milky it may have stretched too much. If it goes back then is should just require some hardener.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: About how thick do you calculate your emulsion to be just prior to exposure?

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
I measured it at 9um with a micrometer focussing knob on a microscope (used a web cam to determine correct focus to cancel out any focussing of the eye during this test).

I then confirmed the thickness with a normal micrometer.

This thickness was made with mold coating. The thickness of the scotch tape was 60um, and the concentration of the gelatin was 12g%.

After developing to narrowband, the thickness was 7um. So a shrinkage of 20%. I then measured the re-play wavelength with a hobby spectroscope at around 510nm. This confirmed my calculations with the amount of chemicals that were present in the gelatin before coating. (I used a bit much chemicals in my original formula. I still need to update the Wiki for green re-play).
